```{r Libraries}

library(tidyverse) # for general stuff
library(factoextra) # for clustering
library(cluster) # for clustering
library(mclust) # for more clustering specifically the arandi
library(data.table) # for faster writing to csv
```

```{r Functions}

# m - number of rows in total - must be divisible by K
# n - number of dimensions for the dataset (number of columns)
# N - noise dimensions to be added to the dataset 'in post' of the generation
# k - clusters to generate
# Overlap - boolean variable, whether the variances of each cluster should be inflated s.t. they overlap, or should they be well-separated?
simple_data <- function(m, n, N, k, overlap) {
  
  # make sure nothing's gonna break
  stopifnot(
    is.logical(overlap), 
    m %% k == 0
  )
  
  # check some options based on our arguments
  if (overlap == TRUE) {
    p_var <- rep(0.5, k) 
  } else {
    p_var <- rep(0.2, k)
  }
  
  # initialise entire result matrix
  rowtotal <- m
  coltotal <- n + N + 1
  
  result <- matrix(0, nrow = rowtotal, ncol = coltotal)
  
  # and initialise the noise that we'll add in
  if (N > 0) {
    all_the_noise <- matrix(rnorm(rowtotal * N, mean = 0, sd = 0.3), 
                            nrow = rowtotal,
                            ncol = N)
  }
  
  # create centre data as separate matrices in 'unmerged'
  for (i in 1:k) {
    cat("generating cluster ", i, "... \n")
    
    row_start <- (i - 1) * m / k + 1
    row_end <- i * m / k
    
    # add in the signal bit
    result[row_start:row_end, 1:n] <- rnorm(m / k * n, i, p_var[[i]])
    
    # add in the noise bit
    if (N > 0) {
      result[row_start:row_end, (n + 1):(n + N)] <- all_the_noise[row_start:row_end, ]
    }
    
    # add in the tag
    result[row_start:row_end, coltotal] <- i
    
    cat("finished cluster ", i, "... \n")
  }
  
  cat("finished all clusters... \n")
  
  # convert it to data frame
  frame <- as.data.frame(result)
  
  names(frame)[1:n] <- paste0("dim", 1:n)
  if (N != 0) {
    names(frame)[(n + 1):(n + N)] <- paste0("noise", 1:N)
  }
  
  names(frame)[ncol(frame)] <- "Tag"
  
  return(frame)
  
}

# uses simple_data to slice, cluster and format a passed dataset. The output is a frame of clusterings that should change based on the dimension, and ideally get worse based on dimension. We are going up to dimension 10 000 here and praying that is enough to show the curse of dimensionality. 
slice_cluster_dataset <- function(data, v, true_k = NULL) {
  # data - dataset to be sliced n scored
  # v - vector of dimension numbers to take arandi score at
  # true_k - true number of clusters. if left unpassed, gap statistic will be used to estimate
  
  # initialise output frame
  frame_out <- tibble(
    Cell_ID = rownames(data),
    True_Labels = data$Tag
  )
  
  #drop the tag col 
  data_no_tag <- data[, colnames(data) != "Tag"]
  
  # slice the dataset, use true k, then save out the clustering
  for (i in seq_along(v)) {
    
    # slice:
    current_slice <- data_no_tag[, 1:v[i], drop = FALSE] # changed to v[i]
    cat(v[i], "dimensions done slicing... \n")
    
    kmobject <- kmeans(current_slice, 
                       centers = true_k,
                       iter.max = 20,
                       nstart = 25)
    
    frame_out[[paste0("Clust", v[i])]] <- kmobject$cluster
    
    cat("Dimension", v[i], "done clustering \n")
    
    
  }
  
  return(frame_out)
  
}



```

```{r Creating Datasets}

# m consistent across all sets. cluster size varying. 3 at 3 clusters, 4 at 4, 3 at 5. 
# creating a dataframe with these parameters to store alongside as a (very) primitive attempt at a metadata file

metadata <- tibble(
  
  index = numeric(),
  name = character(),
  m = numeric(),
  n = numeric(),
  N = numeric(),
  k = numeric(),
  overlap = logical()
  
)

generation_parameters <- list(
  
  list(1, "set01", 1200, 10, 10^5 - 10, 3, TRUE),
  list(2, "set02", 1200, 10, 10^5 - 10, 3, TRUE),
  list(3, "set03", 1200, 10, 10^5 - 10, 3, FALSE),
  list(4, "set04", 1200, 10, 10^5 - 10, 4, TRUE),
  list(5, "set05", 1200, 10, 10^5 - 10, 4, TRUE),
  list(6, "set06", 1200, 10, 10^5 - 10, 4, FALSE),
  list(7, "set07", 1200, 10, 10^5 - 10, 4, FALSE),
  list(8, "set08", 1200, 10, 10^5 - 10, 5, TRUE),
  list(9, "set09", 1200, 10, 10^5 - 10, 5, TRUE),
  list(10, "set10", 1200, 10, 10^5 - 10, 5, FALSE)
  
)

for (i in 1:length(generation_parameters)) {
  for (j in 1:ncol(metadata)) {
    
    metadata[i,j] <- generation_parameters[[i]][j]
  }
}

if (file.exists("D:/KMeansCurseSimTestSet/metadata_kmcs")) {
  cat("Metadata_kmcs already exists... \n")
} else {
  fwrite(metadata, file = "D:/KMeansCurseSimTestSet/metadata_kmcs")
  cat("Written out metadata_kmcs")
}

```

we are kinda seeing that it takes ~20s to make each data set. so let's keep a running estimate of how this works. but yeah now we want to write these out to the appropriate folder along with the metadata file. 

```{r Generation Loop Itself Estimating K}

metadata <- fread("D:/KMeansCurseSimTestSet/Metadata_kmcs")
set.seed(1618)

for (i in 1:10) {
  
  start_time <- Sys.time()
  
  if (file.exists(paste0("D:/KMeansCurseSimTestSet/", metadata[i, "name"][[1]]))) {
    cat("File for ", i, "already exists... \n")
  } else {
    
    cat("Making a file in place of the", i, "th one... \n")
  
    #only make the data if it doesn't already exist
    temp_set <- do.call(simple_data, metadata[i, 3:7])
    cat("made some data, ", i, " \n")
    
    end_time <- Sys.time()
    runtime <- end_time - start_time
    
    cat("it took ", runtime, " to make that data \n")
    
    fwrite(temp_set, file = paste0("D:/KMeansCurseSimTestSet/", metadata[i, "name"][[1]]))
    cat("written out the ", i, "th file \n")
  }
  
  end_time <- Sys.time()
  runtime <- end_time - start_time
  
  cat("it took", runtime, "for that whole loop... \n")
  
}


```
